payload.title: semantic suspicion must not veto authorized work
payload.body: The operator's actual target is recurring false refusals of authorized actions, not expanded persona-launch or skill-delivery work. Evidence in this session includes purview denying route withdrawal and native-process hosting as dispatcher-written specs, and denying a read-only recall tool device because its transport was named Write. Existing semantic judges guess whether an act fits a natural-language role contract and turn that guess into a hard veto. Correct design must separate enforcement of machine-verifiable authority/effect invariants from advisory interpretation of semantic intent: an LLM concern is not proof of a violation and must not override established operator authorization. Human intentions need not all become machine-checkable; those that cannot be checked must not be falsely presented as enforceable predicates. Preserve real objective protections and operator control. Stop the persona-owned-enforcement plan while the holder rectifies this goal; do not fix the problem through more prompt exceptions or an unrelated skill-delivery overhaul. Shared skills and references can already satisfy complete agent composition without physical per-agent duplication or eager body injection.
